title: Epic: VM-native Little Mester agent and isolated workload environment
objective: CURRENT RELEASE COORDINATOR (2026-11-01): deliver the VM-first Little Mester release, preserve the Docker fallback as ./lab-docker, simplify and correct maintained docs, and do not claim merge-ready until code, host acceptance, docs, CI and PR evidence are complete. Follow the phased CURRENT RELEASE PLAN appended to tests.needed; newest phase pointer supersedes stale handoffs. Current owner-configured default guest recursion policy is depth 0 / max 2; host/KVM and release evidence remain separately scoped.

comments.author: cli
comments.body:
ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (2026-10-26).

A1 — Topology chosen and recorded in docs/DECISIONS.md: a full Linux VM running Docker + opencode, or a remote Docker daemon used from the dev container. Record the isolation trade-offs and why the Little Mester repo itself is never the test target.

A2 — Fresh provisioning is one documented command/runbook from a clean host: installs Docker (and NVIDIA container toolkit when GPU is enabled), checks out the repo, and builds the agent image. A CPU-only mode works without a GPU.

A3 — ./verify-lab.sh (or its replacement) passes from a clean clone on the new host, including image build, compose health checks, and the no-host-ports check.

A4 — A disposable test workspace can be created outside the repo checkout (workspaces/test-<id> or a fresh clone), and ./lab <workspace> --unsafe-recurse starts with the agent able to write only inside that workspace.

A5 — Every tooling command is exercised against the disposable workspace and its documented effect observed: lab up/down/stop, docker compose ps/port, ticket-engine create/update/archive/audit/validate, scripts/regen-configs, scripts/verify-metrics.sh, and the mester_tickets_* MCP tools from a live session. "Observed" means the expected file, service, port, or exit code, not just a zero exit.

A6 — Negative cases are tested: the self-mapping guard blocks the repo without --unsafe-recurse; no host ports are published; a stale lock and an orphan file each make validate exit 1 without deleting anything.

A7 — Teardown removes containers, networks, volumes, and the disposable workspace; git status --short in the repo is empty afterwards.

A8 — The repo checkout is never the test target, so destructive cases cannot damage the developer's working tree.

A9 — CI (or a committed pre-merge script) runs the engine/CLI/MCP suites and the lab smoke test in the VM/Docker environment, with results recorded on this ticket before merge.

HUMAN VM ADOPTION PLAN — current handoff, 2026-10-28 (supersedes older proposed PostgreSQL-first/switch-over handoffs). Follow child tickets #41/#42/#43/#45/#50 for subsystem steps; record host results here and on the implementing child ticket through MCP. No separate plan document.

0. WORKING MODE / SAFETY. Use ./lab (host Docker) for actual development now. Keep the working container/session and its auth intact. Do not run ./lab stop, recreate that container, export/import credentials, or edit the same checkout from both agents. The VM may remain provisioned, but do not use it for real changes while model/TUI features are broken. Any VM retry uses the existing overlay; no --clean, stop, or down except the final disposable-VM lifecycle test. Before any action that recreates the Docker container, follow #45 and privately export/verify credentials; this is not needed merely to test the standalone VM.

1. PATCH READY. Before asking the owner to retry, commit/share the targeted code and confirm host checkout contains that revision (git status --short; git log -1 --oneline). Local tests/docs and ticket validation must pass. Do not ask for a fresh install to test a host-only/config change.

2. LOCAL MODEL TRANSPORT FIRST (#42 A8/#41 A5). Check host Docker Engine version is >=28. Check host ports 8080/11434 are not unexpectedly occupied; run docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.vm-model-api.yaml --profile vm-model-api config --quiet, then opt in with docker compose -f compose.yaml -f compose.vm-model-api.yaml --profile vm-model-api up -d ollama-vm-api llamacpp-vm-api. Confirm listeners are on 127.0.0.1 only and not reachable from a separate LAN host. This adds only explicit model APIs; it must not recreate the active host agent. On the existing VM run ./lab-vm up --debug --unsafe-recurse --auto-accept (no --clean), then ./lab-vm status and ./lab-vm ssh; from guest test Ollama /api/tags, llama.cpp /health and /v1/models, then request an actual completion in OpenCode TUI using the configured default model. Expected: a valid response, not Malformed_HTTP_Response; QEMU restrict=on unchanged. If bind conflicts, remote/LAN access, no healthy service, malformed response, or host-Docker disruption occurs, STOP: do not kill/recreate services or widen networking; preserve redacted diagnostics, return to ./lab, and record results. Repeat lab-vm up only after relevant host code/config changes that need syncing or when the VM is stopped; ordinary launches use ./lab-vm agent and do not reinstall.

3. CORE TUI FEATURES (#42 A9/A10). Only after model requests work: fix and verify host metrics UI/tool through a narrow VM path, then verify Ctrl-C prompts, cancel stays, confirm exits, and plugins load. No cutover if any feature is absent.

4. NATIVE CLOUD AUTH (#45). Do not try to make Docker's current OpenAI login count as VM auth and do not copy the Docker database into the guest. Keep Docker session/auth as rollback. In the VM, implement and test the currently supported OpenCode browser OAuth callback to the guest server, one provider request, cancellation/occupied callback-port cases, and persistence across VM restart using #45. Never print or commit codes/tokens. Do not recreate the existing Docker container; export its auth privately only before a future recreation. If VM browser login or persistence fails, stay on Docker.

5. PERMISSIONS (#50). After local model/TUI and auth gates: record guest OpenCode version/mode/argv; verify a harmless allowed tool does not prompt under requested auto mode and a narrow explicit deny remains denied. Do not add blanket allow rules.

6. WORKLOAD (#42/#43). Only when the VM agent is usable: run the disposable PostgreSQL Compose up/health/query/stop/restart/query/down loop from a scratch guest directory with no host port publication. Verify guest Docker/Compose and no agent container. Then complete guest boundary/egress checks and nested-VM capability/boot test (or record a clear unsupported result).

7. LIFECYCLE / CUTOVER (#41/#35). On a separate disposable VM/workspace—not the current valuable overlay—run base→up→status→ssh→agent→Compose→stop→down; verify residue and workspace safety. Keep ./lab available as rollback. Switch active work only after steps 2–7 pass and a real VM session completes a small disposable task; keep Docker/auth intact until VM credential persistence is demonstrated. Any gate failure means stop, use ./lab, preserve evidence and update tickets before another retry.
Child #52 launcher/mode/metrics/recursion gates are complete before changing ./lab default; retain the host-Docker workflow as rollback.

RELEASE ORDER — ACCEPTANCE, DEFAULT, THEN PR MERGE (2026-10-30): (1) Keep host-Docker as the working/default path and preserve the current host session/auth. Finish the exact current #41 handoff first: egress-reload once, then models status only if reload succeeds; child ticket stop conditions control. (5) Only after all parent #35 gates and owner review pass, switch `./lab` to VM-first while retaining verified `./lab-docker` rollback; run clean-workspace smoke and confirm normal warm launch avoids provisioning. (6) Finally update/push the PR branch, require all CI/review checks, record host acceptance and ticket validation, and merge the GitHub PR only after the default-switch smoke passes. Any failed gate means stay on host-Docker, preserve state/evidence, and update the owning ticket before retry. Exact live commands and stop conditions remain on #41/#42/#43/#45/#50/#52; this plan does not authorize a host restart or teardown.

The outer VM likewise runs current CLI/proxy source from its virtiofs workspace, so after local changes sync the relevant files into the ACTIVE stable safe snapshot; do not rebuild/recreate the Docker agent or default VM for source changes. If any future action recreates the host Docker container, follow #45 private auth export first.

Child proxy must apply its own permission/domain policy then relay public HTTP/CONNECT through the existing parent egress proxy endpoint; preserve parent proxy's public-only, mixed-DNS, private/host-route checks, QEMU restrict=on, and no allowlist/network broadening. (2) Add local regression coverage for HTTP and CONNECT chaining, child policy denial before upstream, parent 403 passthrough, and top-level no-chain behavior; run VM Python/Bats/docs/syntax/ticket validation. PASS only if cloud-init is status=done/extended_status=done/errors=[]/recoverable_errors={}, readiness exits 0, child context is depth 1/max 1, one depth-2 launch refuses before state/startup, and returning to the outer guest proves its workspace/session usable. (5) Only after that bounded boot gate, complete #43's separate nested positive-proxy and direct/private/host negative isolation checks; do not infer them from apt success. Keep ERRCONN/model investigation deferred until owner-requested recursion gate is complete. No down/stop/recursion-clean or --clean until evidence is recorded and a separate disposable cleanup gate is approved.

CURRENT RELEASE PLAN — 2026-11-01, owner-directed phased tracker. This supersedes earlier handoffs where they conflict. Maintain progress here through MCP as phases advance, put subsystem evidence on #41/#42/#43/#45/#50/#52 and docs #6, and keep merge/auto-merge/main changes owner-only.
PHASE 0 — Preserve/baseline: retain the existing dirty source and MCP ticket work; run baseline nested-proxy/snapshot regressions; commit a coherent checkpoint and record SHA. No reset or deletion.

PHASE 1 — Runtime/recursion: verify actual tool context and persistent policy, KVM device/groups/CPU flag, resources, QEMU/virtiofsd, Docker/Compose and Node/MCP versions. Current configured cap is depth0/max2. Test a fresh agent sees the same policy and depth3 is rejected before state/QEMU. A KVM/context check is not a nested boot.

PHASE 2 — Release-blocking code: propagate supported permission modes to guest OpenCode; address persistent identity, private state/snapshot secrets and revision verification, resource budgeting, nested runtime prerequisites. Test-first, narrow commits; no broad state deletion or host network changes.

PHASE 3 — Product/docs: simplify and correct README, SECURITY, setup, workflows, VM architecture, product decisions and instructions. Make ./lab VM-first only with explicit command routing and preserve Docker as ./lab-docker. Document current lifecycle effects and distinguish implementation from acceptance evidence.

PHASE 4 — Local release gates: full Bats, VM Python, MCP npm/package under supported Node, exact CI ShellCheck/Ruff, cloud-init schema, docs/link checks, ticket validation and clean diff. Commit each coherent passing slice.

PHASE 5 — Recursive proof at cap2: after resource preflight, prove depth1/depth2 child policy and depth3 refusal before state/QEMU; record SHA, source hash/manifest, exact commands, real status/output/artifacts; verify parent usable. Demonstrate intentional fail→fix→fresh child pass and evidence collection; cleanup only after retaining evidence. Mocks do not replace live VM proof.

PHASE 6 — Remaining acceptance/merge readiness: real model/TUI/metrics, native auth lifecycle, actual allow/deny permissions, guest Compose, outer/child isolation, safe lifecycle, clean-clone and CI/PR/main review. If any required host/human gate remains open, mark BLOCKED with exact evidence; owner merges.

USER-DIRECTED MEMORY WORK (2026-11-01): implement in this order: (1) `./lab-vm resize <profile> <GiB>` for only QEMU profiles owned by that host invocation, with graceful shutdown/restart and preservation of overlay/base/seed/keys/workspace/installed state; (2) new-profile default 8 GiB at depth 0, then 4/2/1 GiB for nested levels; (3) setup-only `--memory <GiB>` for new profiles. Existing profiles without memory metadata retain legacy 4 GiB until resize. Every path must preflight available/cgroup memory + 512 MiB headroom before snapshots/state/QEMU; resize must account for RAM released after clean shutdown before stopping the guest. No TCG/overcommit fallback.

The current coding shell itself reports MemTotal 3.8 GiB / MemAvailable about 2.8 GiB and is an ancestor KVM guest, not a profile managed by the `lab-vm` invocation in this shell. User authorizes 32 GiB for this shell VM but `lab-vm` cannot resize its ancestor; this requires parent hypervisor/launcher configuration and restart. Do not claim the shell has been resized or try a 32-GiB QEMU launch here. Keep general VM acceptance open until the owner has done the external resize and evidence is observed.

Owner-host acceptance remains open: resize a disposable running managed profile on a suitable KVM host, verify graceful shutdown/restart and guest MemTotal, and confirm overlay/base/seed/SSH identity/workspace/installed state remain. This shell cannot resize its ancestor; current MemAvailable is about 2.8 GiB, so do not start a 32-GiB child here.

Next memory phase: implement setup-only `--memory <GiB>` for new profiles, refuse it for existing profiles unless `--clean` explicitly creates a fresh profile, validate and persist the chosen value, and cover parser/preflight/side-effect ordering. Keep host/KVM resize and nested-depth boot acceptance open.

Owner-host acceptance remains open for the three memory phases: on a suitable KVM host, verify fresh depth defaults and an explicit new-profile RAM override in guest MemTotal, warm-start persistence, and managed resize state preservation. The 32-GiB target for the ancestor shell VM requires parent hypervisor/launcher action; do not attempt it as a child VM.
